# SPE round 5 plan: fix F9 with a layout-gated OCR cleanup

Round 4 had one miss. R's Why said "OCR cleanup fixes scanned totals." The tool instead dropped line items on two-column layouts (F9). This round tests one fix for F9. It also tests R's broken Why on the invoices where it should hold.

Assumptions I made from the pasted text:
- The prediction log columns are metric, config, predicted, measured, naive, hit/miss, and closer forecast. The naive forecast is last round's measured value.
- The pasted text does not show the last round 4 requirement ID. I number the new rows R50 to R56. The copy step keeps these numbers if no earlier row uses them.
- The pasted log shows only field accuracy. For every other metric, the cell is the r04 measured value from `spe/prediction-log.md`. It gets copied as a plain number into `r05.yaml` before any trial runs. That copy involves no judgement.
- Trials per invoice, the eval set path, and the grader version all match round 4's Workflow arguments, so the results compare.

## Specify

### Proposals from round 4

| Proposal | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1: keep OCR cleanup but skip it on two-column layouts | Adopt as config S | F9 is open, and F9 is why R missed. S changes one thing from R. |
| P2: add 15 scanned invoices with handwriting | Reject for round 5. Logged as open in `disagreements.md` | Only the AP lead can supply reference fields for the 15 new invoices, and none exist yet. Changing the eval set in the same round as adding S would hide which change moved the score. Q at 0.93 is not a ceiling, because the ceiling rule needs every config at the maximum. |
| P3: drop config P | Adopt | P trails Q on every round 4 metric. No round 5 config builds on P. Dropping P and adding S keeps the run count equal to round 4. |

### Requirements (round 5)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R50 | Config S is R with one change. S calls the OCR cleanup tool only on pages its layout check classifies as single-column. On two-column pages, S passes the raw OCR text to extraction. | r04 F9, proposal P1 | `line_item_recall` on the two-column slice. `gate_vs_manifest` on S's gate log. |
| R51 | S's layout check works from the PDF alone. The agent never reads the layout manifest or the AP lead's reference fields. | Decision: the author does not touch the judge | Leak check at gate 3 finds zero references to the manifest or reference files in agent inputs. |
| R52 | Q and R run unchanged from round 4 as controls. | Respec rule: one change per config | Config hashes for Q and R match r04. |
| R53 | Config P is retired from round 5. Its round 4 rows stay in the log with a "retired r05" note. | Proposal P3 | Workflow `configs` lists only Q, R, and S. |
| R54 | The eval set is the same 60 invoices with the same AP lead reference fields as round 4. | P2 rejection, default D1 | Eval set hash equals r04. |
| R55 | Before any trial runs, each of the 60 invoices gets a layout tag (single-column or two-column) and a scan tag (scanned or native) in `spe/evals/manifest/layout-r05.csv`. The grader alone reads this file. | r04 F9 | Gate 0 counts 60 rows. The two F9 invoices are tagged two-column. |
| R56 | The grader reports total-field accuracy on scanned single-column invoices for each config. This tests R's round 4 Why directly. | r04 prediction log, R row miss | `total_match` on the scanned single-column slice. |

### Defaults (user can override next round)

| ID | Default | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | P2 deferred. It becomes open row "handwriting slice" in `disagreements.md`. The deciders are the user and the AP lead. | It needs reference fields that only the AP lead can provide. |
| D2 | Claude tags the layout manifest from page images before any config runs. The tag list is included in the predict commit so the user can spot-check it. | The tags are eval-side data, and no agent output exists yet when they are made. |
| D3 | The budget cap is 1.5 times the round 4 actual spend. | The run count equals round 4. |

## Predict

Each number starts from round 4's measured value. A number moves only when a Why gives a reason. For the new config S, the naive forecast is its parent R's round 4 value.

| Metric | Grader check | Q | R | S | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Field accuracy, all 60 | `field_match` | 0.93 ± 0.03 | 0.88 ± 0.03 | 0.93 ± 0.03 | Q and R are unchanged. S removes the F9 loss on two-column pages, and those pages then match Q. I add no gain for scanned totals because R showed none in r04. |
| Line-item recall, two-column slice | `line_item_recall` | r04 Q ± 0.05 | r04 R ± 0.05 | r04 Q ± 0.05 | S sends two-column pages down the same path as Q. |
| Total accuracy, scanned single-column slice | `total_match` | r04 Q ± 0.05 | r04 R ± 0.05 | r04 R ± 0.03 | S runs the same cleanup as R on these pages. If R beats Q here, R's Why holds where F9 does not apply. |
| PO mismatch flag accuracy, all 60 | `po_flag_match` | r04 Q ± 0.03 | r04 R ± 0.03 | r04 Q ± 0.04 | Flags depend on totals and line items. F9 is the only known source of R's loss. |
| Layout gate agreement with manifest (S only) | `gate_vs_manifest` | n/a | n/a | 0.97 ± 0.03 | Single-column versus two-column is a coarse call. I expect at most 2 of 60 invoices to be misread. |

Stop-rule status: round 4 had a miss, so the streak of matched rounds is 0. Round 5 can bring it to 1 at most.

## Evaluate

### After approval, in order

1. Save the pasted text and "go again" word for word to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md`. Add the round 5 table to `spec.md`. Add D1 to `disagreements.md`. Mark P as retired. Commit locally: `spe(r05): specify`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml` from the Predict table, with r04 values resolved to numbers. Write the layout manifest. Commit locally: `spe(r05): predict`. The yaml is not edited after this commit.
3. Run the gates below. Then launch the Workflow.

### Gates (halt and report on any failure)

| Gate | Step | Pass condition |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Check the layout manifest | 60 rows. Every row has both tags. Both F9 invoices are tagged two-column. |
| 1 | Grader selftest, with fixtures for the new slice checks and `gate_vs_manifest` | All checks pass. |
| 2 | Regrade round 4 Q and R outputs with the round 5 grader as a control | Field accuracy reproduces 0.93 for Q and 0.88 for R exactly. Any other value means the grader is broken. |
| 3 | Leak check on S's tool and prompt inputs | No path or content from the manifest or the reference fields appears. |
| 4 | Dry run: 2 invoices (one F9 two-column invoice and one scanned single-column invoice) × Q, R, S × 1 trial | All 6 runs finish and grade. S's gate log shows a skip on the two-column invoice and a cleanup on the scanned invoice. |

### Workflow arguments

```json
{
  "round": "r05",
  "script": "spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js",
  "configs": ["Q", "R", "S"],
  "eval_set": "same path and hash as r04",
  "trials_per_invoice": "same as r04",
  "grader_manifest": "spe/evals/manifest/layout-r05.csv",
  "predictions": "spe/predictions/r05.yaml",
  "out": "spe/evals/results/r05/",
  "budget_cap": "1.5 x r04 actual spend"
}
```

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

The trial run count equals round 4's, at 3 configs × 60 invoices × the r04 trial count. The dry run adds 6 runs. The regrade control uses the grader only. S adds one layout check per page. My estimate is 1.0 to 1.1 times round 4's actual spend. This is not measured.

### Halt conditions

- Spend reaches the 1.5x budget cap.
- The leak check or any run shows the answer key in agent inputs.
- The grader selftest fails, or the regrade control does not reproduce round 4.
- A decision only the user can make comes up. For example, if the AP lead sends handwriting references mid-run, they wait for round 6.

### After the run

Add the r05 rows to `prediction-log.md` with hit or miss for each cell. Update F9 to fixed or still open based on the two-column slice. Log any new failure as F10 onward. Write the "Proposed for round 6" table, with P2 carried forward as open. Commit locally: `spe(r05): evaluate`, then `spe(r05): learn`. All commits stay local. Nothing is pushed.
critiques: The answer is titled "SPE round 5 plan" and opens with a Specify phase. That phase reviews the round 4 proposals and writes new requirements. The agent treated "go again" as a respec for round 5 without being told the phase.

The Proposals table gives a decision and a reason for each one. P1 is adopted as config S because F9 is open. P2 is rejected for round 5 because no AP lead references exist and the change would confound S. P3 is adopted because P trails Q on every metric.

R50, R55, and R56 cite "r04 F9" or the r04 prediction log miss. R53 and R54 trace to the P3 and P2 decisions. R51 and R52 cite process rules and are guards for the F9 fix. The substantive new requirements are tied to F9 and round 4 evidence.

The Predict section says "Each number starts from round 4's measured value" and uses R's r04 value as the naive baseline for S. Every cell has a band, for example "0.93 ± 0.03" and "r04 R ± 0.05". Many cells are placeholders, and the slice metrics may not have r04 values yet. The method and the bands are still there, and the assumptions state the placeholders resolve to numbers before trials.

Each metric row has a Why column with a specific reason. One example is "S removes the F9 loss on two-column pages, and those pages then match Q." The gate-agreement row explains why 0.97 is expected.

Step 2 writes `spe/predictions/r05.yaml` from the Predict table and commits it as `spe(r05): predict`. It also says the yaml "is not edited after this commit." Gates and the Workflow run only in step 3, after that commit.

The Gates table runs in order before the full run. Gate 1 is a grader selftest. Gate 2 regrades round 4 Q and R outputs as a control that must reproduce 0.93 and 0.88. Gate 4 is a 6-run dry run. Gates 0 and 3 add a manifest check and a leak check.
